title: Briefing: France's protests escalate, plus Italy and Albania
script: This is the Unowned briefing for Monday, October nineteenth. It's read by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our checked timelines.

French high school students have blockaded schools since September over teacher shortages and crumbling buildings, and nationwide protests on Saturday turned violent in several cities. Paris police say they arrested a record eight hundred fifty-five people; that's reported so far by one source. They also say a man died after collapsing during the protests; that's reported so far by one source. What's next: final arrest and injury figures, and whether more protests are planned.

Students and cost-of-living protesters marched in cities across Italy on Friday and Saturday against Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government, with clashes in Turin, Milan and Bologna. A Rome police union official says eighteen officers were hurt by firecrackers, smoke bombs, stones and bottles outside the Education Ministry; that's reported so far by one source. What's next: a general strike called by the CGIL union for November twentieth, and final figures from the weekend.

In Albania, student protests against Prime Minister Edi Rama's government have continued for nearly a week, with riots, arrests, and clashes with police in Tirana. Rama alleges that police neutralized a drone carrying explosives aimed at the prime minister's office, and blames a foreign hand, not students, for the violence. What's next: Saturday's arrest figures, and whether students and the government begin talks.
That's the briefing. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com.
